title: Steady After the Drops

patient.name: Mdm Quek Lai Cheng
patient.presenting_complaint: Elderly patient just dilated for a fundus check; unsteady on her feet and using a walking frame

history.hpc: Mdm Quek, aged 83, has just been dilated. Her vision is now blurry and she is light-sensitive. She uses a walking frame and says: 'My legs not so steady, now the eye also blur, scared I fall.' She is waiting to be seen. The PSA must complete a fall-risk (PFAER) assessment and put active fall-prevention measures in place.
history.pmhx: Osteoarthritis, hypertension. Previous fall at home last year.
history.social_hx: Lives with a domestic helper who is with her today. Uses a walking frame.

examination_findings.fundus: To be examined by doctor now that pupils are dilated

investigations.fall_risk_assessment: Fall-risk (PFAER) assessment: high risk identified — advanced age (>80), reduced baseline vision now worsened by dilation, photosensitivity, mobility impairment (walking frame, osteoarthritis), and a previous fall. Although accompanied by a helper, active measures are needed.
investigations.va_distance: RE and LE 6/18 pre-dilation, both now blurred.

diagnosis: High fall risk on PFAER assessment: an elderly, mobility-impaired patient with reduced and now further-blurred vision after dilation. The PSA competency is completing the fall-risk assessment and taking active prevention measures, not just documenting the risk.

immediate: Complete the PFAER fall-risk assessment and identify the multiple risk factors
Do not let her walk unaided; accompany her and ensure she uses her walking frame
Seat her safely in a well-lit area near the station where she can be observed
Offer sunglasses/UV protectors for the post-dilation photosensitivity
Ensure the helper stays with her and inform the nurse that she is high fall risk
Document the fall-risk assessment and the actions taken
follow_up: Doctor to proceed with the dilated fundus examination
Ensure she is escorted for the rest of the visit and on the way out
Flag in records that she is high fall risk, especially when dilated
patient_education: Explain her vision will be blurry and light-sensitive for about 4-6 hours after the drops
Advise her to move slowly with her frame and to ask for help, not to walk alone
Reassure her that staff and her helper will assist her
Advise bringing her frame and a companion to future visits

key_points: Establishes advanced age, mobility impairment, and walking-frame use
Notes the previous fall and reduced baseline vision
Recognises post-dilation blurring/photosensitivity as added acute risk
Confirms whether a companion/helper is present
Completes the PFAER fall-risk assessment at this visit
Identifies the multiple specific risk factors
Recognises dilation has acutely increased the risk
Documents pre-dilation VA and IOP appropriately
Classifies the patient as high fall risk
Recognises the combined chronic and acute (dilation) contributors
Understands high risk requires active measures, not just a note
Does not dismiss the risk because a helper is present
Accompanies the patient and ensures walking-frame use and safe seating
Offers sunglasses and keeps the helper with her
Informs the nurse and documents the assessment and actions
